name: Lighting
controls: Where the light in the graphic world comes from, how hard or soft it is, what color it is and how much contrast it makes: the light model that every gradient, highlight, rim, shadow and glow in the film agrees with.
question: How should the film be lit: flat and graphic, bright and even, or dramatic with real light sources?
notes: Lighting is the most under-specified slot in weak briefs and the one that most separates designed frames from default ones. In code-built motion graphics there is no renderer computing light, so light is painted: a key is a directional gradient overlay, a rim is a thin bright inner edge, a practical is a stacked glow, volumetric light is blurred beams in screen blend, and every drop shadow must fall away from the same key. The rule that makes it read as light rather than decoration: one motivated source per scene with a stated direction and color temperature, and everything agrees with it (shadows, highlights, gradients, reflections). Name the light by source and direction ('key from upper-left, warm; cool rim from behind right'), never by mood ('dramatic lighting'). Pick at most two: usually one setup or contrast key (high-key, low-key, three-point) plus one quality or source (golden hour, neon practicals, volumetric). Overlaps: shadow (its own dimension) is the shape of the shadow; lighting decides where it falls and how dark it is. color-grade is the global transform applied after lighting (film stock, contrast curve, split tone); lighting is local and directional. effects holds one-off optical events (bloom, lens flare, light streaks); here they are only consequences of a source. Color temperatures are given in kelvin as a guide for hex choice: tungsten 3200K reads #ffc58f-#ffd9a8, daylight 5600K neutral #fff8f0, overcast 6500-7500K #eef3ff, blue hour 9000K+ #9fb8ff. In a HyperFrames build, lighting layers are ordinary elements (gradients, masks, blend modes) inside the #world wrapper so camera moves carry them; any flicker or drift is seeded and driven by the paused GSAP timeline, never CSS animations or Math.random. Full-frame blurs are expensive: pre-blur static light layers once or keep blur radii under 40px at 1080p.

families.name: Natural light and time of day

options.what: No simulated light at all: color fields and shapes carry the image, with at most a single consistent shadow direction.
options.looks: Solid fills, no gradients implying light, no highlights or rims; any shadows are flat, hard or offset and all point the same way.
options.motion: Light never changes because there is none; drama comes from color switches, scale and cuts.
options.use: Swiss, flat design, neo-brutalism, kinetic typography, explainers, most UI and data films.
options.conveys: Clarity, graphic confidence, honesty; nothing pretends to be physical.
options.vs: High-key is bright light with soft shadows on objects that have volume; flat graphic has no light and no volume at all.
options.prompt: Use no light model: flat fills only, no gradients that imply a light source, no highlights, rims, glows or vignettes. If the style uses shadows, every shadow is the same flat offset (for example 0.8% of frame height down-right, 0 blur, ink at 100% or 20% opacity) in every scene. Get emphasis from color, scale and position, never from light.

options.what: The standard rig: a main key light, a weaker fill from the opposite side, and a rim (back) light that separates the subject from the background.
options.looks: Subjects have a lit side and a softer shadow side (key-to-fill about 2:1 to 4:1) and a thin bright edge on the side away from the key; background slightly darker than the subject.
options.motion: The rig stays fixed while the camera and objects move, so highlights slide across surfaces as they turn.
options.use: Product heroes, UI cards and devices with volume, 3D objects, mascots, premium SaaS films.
options.conveys: Polish, dimensionality, a considered commercial finish.
options.vs: High-key lowers the key-to-fill ratio until shadows almost vanish; low-key removes most of the fill; three-point sits in between and always has the rim.
search: key fill rim light motion design
options.prompt: Light every scene with one fixed three-point rig. Key from upper-left (about 10 o'clock, 45 degrees): a linear-gradient overlay on each subject from #fff1e0 to transparent across 60% of its width, 12-18% opacity, soft-light blend. Fill from the right at a third of the key (key-to-fill about 3:1): a #e3ebff gradient at 5-8%. Rim on the edge away from the key: a 1-2px bright inner edge (inset box-shadow or a masked gradient stroke) at 40-60% white. Background 10-20% darker than the subject's lit side. Every drop shadow falls down-right, away from the key (offset 0.6-1% of frame height, blur 2-3x the offset). Camera moves never change the light direction.

options.what: Bright, low-contrast light with very soft or no visible shadows and mostly light tones.
options.looks: Light backgrounds (often near-white), soft contact shadows only, key-to-fill near 1:1 to 2:1, no deep blacks except in type.
options.motion: Clean, airy; objects appear to float in soft light, shadows barely shift as they move.
options.use: Consumer apps, health, education, friendly SaaS, Apple-style white product frames.
options.vs: Overcast soft is diffuse natural light with a cool cast and slightly lower brightness; high-key is controlled, bright and neutral.
options.prompt: Light high-key: backgrounds between #f4f4f2 and #ffffff (never pure #fff for large fields; use #fafaf8), key-to-fill about 1.5:1, so shadow sides are only 5-10% darker. Shadows are soft contact shadows only: blur 3-5% of the object's height, 8-14% opacity, offset nearly straight down. No vignette, no rims, no deep blacks except type and the product's own dark parts. Keep text contrast at 4.5:1 by using a dark ink (#111-#222), not by darkening the scene.

options.what: Dark, high-contrast light: most of the frame falls into shadow and only the subject is picked out by a strong key.
options.looks: Near-black surroundings (#0b0b0d-#15151a), a single pool or slash of light on the subject, key-to-fill 8:1 or more, deep shadow sides.
options.motion: Reveals happen by light: subjects move into the key, a light sweeps across, or the pool widens.
options.use: Premium hardware, dramatic reveals, security, finance, film-trailer-style launches, noir.
options.vs: Silhouette lights only the background and leaves the subject black; low-key lights the subject and leaves the background black.
options.prompt: Light low-key: background #0b0b0d to #15151a with a subtle radial falloff (center 4-6% lighter than the corners). One hard key per scene, usually from high side (about 60-75 degrees off axis): a radial or elliptical gradient pool on the subject, lit side up to 80-90% of full brightness, shadow side no brighter than 12%. No fill. Optional 1px rim at 30-50% on the far edge to hold the silhouette. Reveal the hero by sweeping or widening the pool (0.8-1.2s, power2.inOut) rather than fading it in. Text sits in the lit area or in white on black at full contrast.

options.what: A single hard light from 90 degrees to the side, so the subject is cut into a lit half and a dark half.
options.looks: A sharp terminator line down the middle of objects and faces; strong texture raking across surfaces; long sideways shadows.
options.motion: Turning objects show the terminator sliding across them; a light that rakes across a surface reveals its texture.
options.use: Hardware and material close-ups, bold typographic scenes, tension beats, before/after splits.
options.vs: Three-point softens the shadow side with fill; split light leaves it dark. Rim light hits the edge from behind, not the side.
options.prompt: Light from hard 90-degree side (left by default): on each subject a linear gradient at 90 degrees with a sharp transition (stops at 48% and 52%) from lit (#ffffff at 20-30% soft-light) to shadow (#000 at 35-50% multiply). Shadows are long and horizontal: offset 3-6% of frame width to the right, blur under 1% of frame height. Raised surfaces and embossed type catch a 1px highlight on their left edges only. Keep the direction identical in every scene.

options.what: The light is behind the subject, so the subject reads as a dark shape against a bright background.
options.looks: Solid dark shapes with crisp outlines against a bright field or glow; optional thin light spill wrapping the edges.
options.motion: Shape and pose carry everything; motion must read in outline, so gestures are broad and profiles clear.
options.use: Reveals of a product's shape, iconic openers, music and lifestyle pieces, storytelling with anonymous figures.
options.vs: Low-key keeps a lit subject in a dark world; silhouette is a dark subject in a bright world.
options.prompt: Backlight the scene: the background is the brightest area (a flat accent field or a radial glow, center at 100%, falling to 60% at the edges). The subject is a solid dark shape (#0a0a0a or the darkest brand ink) with no internal detail. Add a 1-3px light wrap on the outline (a blurred copy of the background color at 40-60% behind the edge, 2-4px blur). Poses and outlines must read at thumbnail size; keep the subject's profile unambiguous.

options.what: Light from behind and to the side that draws a thin bright line along the subject's edges, separating it from a dark background.
options.looks: Dark objects outlined by a crisp bright edge on one or both sides; the body stays mostly in shadow.
options.motion: The rim slides along edges as objects rotate; a rim that tracks a turning device is a premium staple.
options.use: Dark-mode product films, devices and 3D objects on black, logo reveals, tech and automotive-style launches.
options.vs: Silhouette leaves the whole subject black with a bright background; rim light keeps the background dark and lights only the edge.
options.prompt: Rim-light subjects on a dark background (#0c0c0f-#16161b): on each subject add a 1-2px bright inner edge on the side away from camera-left (inset box-shadow -1px 0 0 rgba(255,255,255,.6) or a masked linear-gradient stroke fading along the edge), plus a soft outer glow of 6-12px at 10-15% in the same color. The subject body stays at 8-20% brightness. When the subject rotates, move the rim along the edge with the rotation so it stays on the light side. One rim color per film (white, or the brand accent at most).

options.what: A single source directly overhead, lighting the tops of objects and throwing shadows straight down.
options.looks: Bright tops, darkening toward the bottom of each object, short shadows pooled directly underneath; faces get dark eye sockets.
options.motion: Objects rising into the light brighten; objects set down land in their own shadow pool.
options.use: Tabletop product shots, interrogation or tension beats, stage-like single-object scenes.
options.vs: A spotlight pool lights a round area of floor; top light is about how the object itself is lit from above.
options.prompt: Light from directly overhead: every subject gets a vertical linear gradient from lit top (#ffffff at 18-25% soft-light) to shadowed bottom (#000 at 25-40% multiply). Shadows sit directly under objects as flattened ellipses (width 90-110% of the object, height 12-18% of its width, blur 2-4% of frame height, 25-40% opacity) and shrink and darken as objects land. Background darkens toward the bottom of the frame by 10-20%.

options.what: The low, warm sun of the hour after sunrise or before sunset: long soft shadows and amber light with glowing edges.
options.looks: Warm amber key (#ffb26b-#ffd08a) at a low angle, long shadows, backlit edges that glow, a cooler blue-violet fill in shadows, gentle haze.
options.motion: Slow; light may shift warmer over the film, flares and glints come from a low sun position.
options.use: Lifestyle, travel, hopeful turns, brand films, the 'after' state of a before/after.
options.vs: Warm negative film is a grade applied to everything; golden hour is a directional light with a real low sun position.
options.prompt: Light golden hour: a low sun from one side (just above the horizon line, about 10-15 degrees elevation) as a warm key #ffb870 painted with a linear-gradient overlay at 20-30% soft-light; shadows are long (length 2-4x object height, pointing away from the sun), soft (blur 1-2% of frame height) and tinted blue-violet (#3a3f7a at 25-35%). Edges facing the sun get a 2-4px glowing rim (#ffd9a0, 6-10px blur). Add a sun-side radial haze (#ffcf99 at 10-18%, screen). Optional slow warm-shift of 200-400K equivalent across the film via the key overlay's opacity.

options.what: The deep blue ambient light just after sunset or before sunrise, often with warm practical lights starting to glow.
options.looks: Saturated cool blue ambient (#2e3f78-#5b6fb3), soft shadowless light, small warm practicals (#ffc27a) glowing against it.
options.motion: Calm and still; lights switching on one by one is the natural event.
options.use: Night-before-launch moods, city and travel, calm reflective scenes, the quiet beat before a reveal.
options.vs: Day-for-night is a grade that fakes night from day; blue hour is a real (painted) light condition with warm practicals.
options.prompt: Light blue hour: ambient is a soft top-down gradient from #5b6fb3 (sky) to #1f2a52 (ground), no hard shadows (contact shadows only, 15-25%, soft). Place 2-5 warm practicals (#ffc27a windows, lamps, screens), each with a 2-radius glow (inner 6-10px at 80%, outer 30-60px at 20%, screen). Turn practicals on one at a time on beats (0.15-0.3s each, seeded tiny flicker of 1-3% for 2-3 frames on switch-on). Keep text in a warm or white ink with 4.5:1 contrast against the blue.

options.what: Diffuse, shadowless light from an overcast sky: even, cool and gentle.
options.looks: Very soft wraparound light, faint contact shadows, slightly cool neutral cast, low contrast, muted highlights.
options.motion: Nothing in the light moves; calm, documentary steadiness.
options.use: Documentary, editorial, calm healthcare or finance, Scandinavian-minimal brands.
options.vs: High-key is bright and punchy; overcast is diffuse and a little subdued. Avoid it by accident: flat cloudy light is also the default 'AI look' in generated footage, so choose it on purpose.
options.prompt: Light overcast: no directional key; subjects get a very gentle top-to-bottom gradient (top 6-8% lighter, soft-light). Contact shadows only: blur 5-8% of object height, 10-15% opacity, directly under. Cast the scene slightly cool (overlay #eef3ff at 6-10%, soft-light) and keep highlights below pure white (max #f2f2f2 on large surfaces). Contrast comes from ink and color, never from light.

options.what: High, hard midday sun: short, crisp, very dark shadows and bright saturated surfaces.
options.looks: Near-vertical shadows with razor edges, high contrast, saturated colors, bright hot highlights, deep blue skies.
options.motion: Snappy and punchy; shadows are graphic shapes that move with objects.
options.use: Summer, sport, energetic consumer brands, bold pop styles, desert and travel moods.
options.vs: Top light is a studio overhead source with falloff; hard noon is sunlight: shadows are crisp and the whole scene is bright.
options.prompt: Light hard noon: shadows are crisp shapes (0-2px blur) falling almost straight down and slightly right (offset 1-3% of frame height), at 45-60% opacity in a cool dark (#1b2340). Lit surfaces are saturated (boost saturation 10-20% on the world layer) and highlights clip to near-white on edges facing up. Skies or backgrounds use a deep saturated blue or the style's brightest color. No haze, no glow.

options.what: Soft directional daylight from one side through a window, falling off across the room, often with the window's shape cast on surfaces.
options.looks: One side bright and soft, a gradual falloff to darker on the far side, optional window-frame or blind shadows striping surfaces.
options.motion: Slow and domestic; shadows of blinds or frames slide slightly as the camera moves.
options.use: Home, productivity, writing and reading apps, lifestyle, calm storytelling.
options.vs: Three-point is a studio rig; window light is one motivated soft source with natural falloff and no rim.
options.prompt: Light from a window on the left: a broad linear-gradient key across the whole world layer from #fff4e6 at 18-25% (left edge, soft-light) to transparent by 70% of the frame width, plus darkening to #000 at 10-15% multiply at the right edge. Optionally cast the window's shape: 3-5 soft parallelogram bands (skewed 10-20 degrees, blur 1% of frame height, lighten at 8-12%) across surfaces. Shadows fall to the right, soft (blur 1.5-2.5% of frame height).

options.what: Saturated colored light coming from visible neon signs, tubes and screens in a dark environment.
options.looks: A dark scene lit by 1-3 saturated sources (magenta, cyan, red), colored spill on nearby surfaces, glowing tubes, reflections on wet or glossy floors.
options.motion: Occasional seeded flicker or a sign buzzing on; spill color changes as subjects pass sources.
options.use: Nightlife, gaming, music, cyberpunk and synthwave styles, after-dark consumer brands.
options.conveys: Night energy, cool, urban edge, retro-futurism.
options.vs: Colored gels wash a whole scene in color from off-screen lights; neon practicals are visible sources inside the frame. Glowing neon text as decoration is a slop tell; here the light has a source and lights its surroundings.
options.prompt: Light with visible neon practicals in a dark scene (#07070b-#12101a): 1-3 sources in the style's saturated hues (for example #ff2e88 and #29e3ff). Each tube is a 3-6px core in near-white tinted toward its hue, with stacked glows (drop-shadow or text-shadow at 4px 90%, 16px 50%, 48px 20%, same hue). Spill: a radial gradient of the source's hue on nearby surfaces at 15-30% screen, falling off within 20-30% of frame width. Reflections on the floor as a vertically flipped, 8-12px blurred copy at 20-30%. Flicker only on switch-on or once as an event (seeded, 2-4 frames). Never use glow on body text.

options.what: Off-screen lights with colored filters wash the subject in two or more strong hues, usually one from each side.
options.looks: Subjects lit in bold color (magenta key, cyan fill; red and blue), color mixing where the lights overlap, dark shadows in between.
options.motion: Gel colors can switch on the beat for punctuation; a slow hue cross-fade between two gels for mood.
options.use: Music, fashion, nightlife, bold brand films, dramatic tonal shifts.
options.vs: Neon practicals are visible sources in frame; gels are unseen lights that color the subject.
search: red blue gel light motion graphics
options.prompt: Light with two gels: a key gel from one side (for example #ff3d7f) and a contrasting gel from the other (for example #2fb8ff), each as a linear-gradient overlay across the subject from its side, 30-45% in color or overlay blend, meeting in the middle with a 10-20% overlap where the hues mix. Shadows between the gels go deep (#0b0b12). Switch gel colors only on downbeats (hard set, no tween) or cross-fade them over 1.5-3s for a mood change; never cycle continuously.

options.what: Two motivated sources of different color temperature in one scene, typically a warm interior key and a cool daylight or screen spill.
options.looks: One side of the subject warm (#ffcf9e), the other cool (#b9ccff); warm practicals against a cool ambient; natural color contrast without a grade.
options.motion: The balance can shift as a story beat (a cool screen glow gives way to warm morning light).
options.use: Storytelling scenes, home and work settings, films about time of day or mood shifts.
options.vs: Teal-orange grade pushes all shadows teal and all highlights orange globally; mixed lighting assigns warm and cool to real sources with directions.
options.prompt: Light each scene with two motivated sources: a warm key (#ffcf9e, from a named practical such as a lamp, camera-left) as a gradient overlay at 15-22% soft-light, and a cool spill (#b9ccff, from a window or screen, camera-right) at 10-15%. Shadows on the warm side are tinted cool and vice versa. State both sources in the scene notes and keep their sides fixed within a scene.

options.what: The product's own screen is the light source, lighting hands, desk or surroundings in its colors.
options.looks: A dim room, the device or UI as the brightest element, its colors spilling on nearby surfaces; the light changes when the UI changes.
options.motion: When the UI changes state or color, the spill on the surroundings changes on the same frame.
options.use: App and software launches that want a cinematic, human setting; late-night work stories; the product as hero.
options.conveys: The product at the center of someone's world; intimacy, focus.
options.vs: Neon practicals are decorative signs; screen glow is motivated by the product itself.
options.prompt: Make the product screen the only key: surroundings at 8-18% brightness; the screen at full brightness with a spill gradient in the UI's dominant color on adjacent surfaces (radial, 20-35% screen blend, falloff within 25% of frame width) and on the near side of any hands or objects. When the UI changes color or state, update the spill color on the same frame. Keep the UI itself ungraded and exact.

options.what: Visible shafts of light through haze or dust, streaming from a source behind or above the subject.
options.looks: Soft bright beams fanning from a source, dust motes inside the beams, haze lifting the background, subject partly backlit.
options.motion: Beams drift very slowly or intensify at the reveal; motes drift inside the beam only.
options.use: Hero reveals, cinematic brand films, awe moments, spiritual or discovery beats.
options.vs: Bloom is a glow around bright objects; volumetric light is a beam in the air. Used everywhere it becomes slop; use it for one reveal.
options.prompt: Add volumetric light only for the reveal scene: 3-7 beams from one source above-behind the subject, each a blurred linear or conic gradient (source color at 30-40% fading to 0 over 70-90% of frame height, 20-40px blur), screen blend, overall 12-25% so they never hide type. Beams brighten from 0 to target over 0.8-1.2s as the hero appears (power2.out), then hold; drift no more than 1-2 degrees over the shot. Optional 10-30 dust motes inside the beams only (seeded positions, 1-3px, 20-50% opacity, moving 1-3% of frame per second). No beams in other scenes.

options.what: Air between the camera and distant objects: far layers get lighter, lower in contrast and tinted toward the sky color.
options.looks: Receding planes fade into the background color; near objects crisp and saturated, far ones soft and pale.
options.motion: With parallax camera moves, the haze sells depth: far layers move slower and stay pale.
options.use: Layered 2.5D worlds, landscapes, cities, depth reveals, camera journeys.
options.vs: Depth of field blurs out-of-focus planes; haze reduces contrast and tints with distance, even when in focus.
options.prompt: Apply depth haze by plane: for each plane behind the subject, blend toward the background color by 15% per plane (overlay a solid of the background color at 15%, 30%, 45%), reduce contrast (filter: contrast(0.9), 0.8, 0.7) and add 0-2px blur for the farthest. Near planes stay at full contrast and saturation. Keep the haze color consistent with the key light's temperature.

options.what: A single hard-edged circle or ellipse of light on a dark stage, isolating one subject.
options.looks: A crisp or slightly soft oval of light on the floor and subject, darkness everywhere else, a faint cone in haze if present.
options.motion: The spot snaps on with a clunk, follows the subject, or jumps from one subject to the next as focus shifts.
options.use: Isolating one feature among many, awards and stage tropes, a single hero stat, comedic reveals.
options.vs: Low-key is a general dark mood with a sculpting key; a spotlight is a visible, bounded pool that isolates.
options.prompt: Isolate the subject with a spotlight: darken the scene to 10-15% (a full-frame #000 overlay at 85-90%) and cut a hole with a radial-gradient mask (a hard or slightly soft edge: stops 0-92% transparent, 100% opaque; ellipse flattened to 35-45% height on the floor). Snap it on in 1-2 frames with a set() on a downbeat, or move it between subjects over 0.3-0.5s (power3.inOut). Only one spot visible at a time.

options.what: A seamless curved backdrop with large soft boxes: the product floats in an even, controlled studio space with soft reflections.
options.looks: A backdrop that curves from floor to wall without a horizon line, a soft gradient from lighter behind the product to darker at the edges, crisp specular highlights, a soft contact shadow or reflection.
options.motion: Slow orbits or turns of the product, highlights sliding across its surfaces; the backdrop never moves.
options.use: Hardware, devices, packaged goods, app icons or UI cards treated as objects, premium launch heroes.
options.conveys: Premium, precision, focus on the object.
options.vs: High-key is a general brightness level; the studio sweep is a specific set (curved backdrop, softboxes, reflection) for one object.
options.prompt: Stage the product in a studio sweep: background a radial gradient centered 45-55% down (the backdrop's brightest point just behind the product, 8-15% lighter than the edges), no horizon line. Two large soft boxes: a broad key from upper-left and a strip light from the right, painted as long soft highlight bands on the product's surfaces (white at 25-45%, 10-20px blur, clipped to the product). Contact shadow: a soft ellipse under the product (blur 3-6% of its height, 20-30%) or a floor reflection (flipped copy, 25-35% fading to 0 over 30% of its height). Turns and orbits move the highlight bands across surfaces; the backdrop stays fixed.

options.what: A narrow band of highlight travels across a glossy surface, logo or type once, as if a light passed over it.
options.looks: A soft diagonal bright band moving across metal, glass, screen or letterforms, clipped to the object.
options.motion: One pass, 0.4-0.8s, on the moment the object lands or the logo locks up; never on a loop.
options.use: Logo lockups, product reveals, premium card or badge moments, the button at the end.
options.vs: A shimmer loop that repeats is an idle and a slop tell; a specular sweep happens once, motivated by a landing.
options.prompt: Pass one specular sweep over the object at its landing: a linear-gradient band at 20-25 degrees (transparent, white at 55-75%, transparent; band width 12-20% of the object width) clipped to the object (background-clip:text for type, a mask for shapes), translating from -30% to 130% of the object width in 0.5-0.7s with power2.inOut, starting 0.05-0.1s after the object settles. Screen or overlay blend. Once per object per film; never repeated or looped.
